panels.hypothesis: Bounded adaptive allocation improves atomic acquisition per attempted compute.
panels.confound_control: Run only one selected atomic bank first. Variable outcome-dependent group length changes the estimator; it cannot be advertised as unchanged fixed-N MaxRL. Actual NGU requires its policy-age/async controls; this same-snapshot variant is labeled NGU-inspired.

prerequisites: frozen earlier-skill reference and replay-only TRAIN bank
panels.hypothesis: A real preservation loss reduces earlier-skill losses within declared later-skill acquisition cost.
panels.confound_control: Uniform-success centered RL replay supplies zero correctness advantage. Keep a separate preservation loss and preserve the binary acquisition reward; anchor retention and acquired-donor retention use different references.

panels.hypothesis: A calibrated allocation improves donor acquisition versus composition/legacy damage relative to simple masking and attenuation.
panels.confound_control: Retest every masked donor alone and keep the other donor unchanged. A positive row multiplier cannot alter within-row rankings if row keep counts are fixed. The published full-weight F-WANDA method and a two-distribution delta-retention proxy are distinct methods.

panels.hypothesis: Dense qualified supervision creates atomic competence from which binary RL can improve, without silently importing dependent RS training.
panels.confound_control: Central MiMo CE512 mechanics and quarantined environment specifications establish no acquisition effect. Capture discrepancy is fixed or remains blocked; tolerances are not loosened. Distillation, RL and task-vector composition are separate interventions.
